newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Stark rejects rumours of EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Stark rejects rumours of EMU delay.

text.p: Juergen Stark, state secretary in the German Finance Ministry, rejected rumours there would be a postponement to the start of the planned European economic and monetary union (EMU), a German newsletter said on Thursday.
Investment newletter Platow Brief reported Stark as saying rumours that government circles were considering delaying the start of the planned currency union were without foundation.
"I do not understand all this upset in the debate about the fulfillment of the Maastricht criteria or a postponement of the euro," Stark said in a release ahead of publication on Friday.
"We must do our homework and them we can decide at the beginning of 1998 (who fulfills the criteria)," he said.
Stark made similar comments in a speech in New York on Wednesday, when he said he could not understand recent foreign exchange market jitters over a possible EMU delay.
